subject: nineTailedKitsune
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: nine-tailed kitsune fox with spirit flames.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm planning the overall structure for a quadruped fox model, aiming for a manageable yet quality build around 400 lines, and sketching out proportions and the skeleton hierarchy starting from the hip root joint.

Now I'm working out the rest of the skeleton: spine chain, neck chain, head joint, nine tail chains fanned from the rump, ears, legs, and spirit flame decorations at tail tips. I'm defining the body sweep with varying radii from rump to chest, then building the neck chain connecting to the head joint with proper parenting.

For the head, I'm sizing a skull sphere with scale values for width, height, and length, then planning the muzzle as a sweep or cone shape with an upper jaw capsule for the snout structure.

Then I'm defining a separate jaw bone, parented to the head with its own aim and capsule shape, plus a dark nose sphere at the tip—needing to explicitly specify bones since positions alone could confuse the head/jaw assignment. For eyes, I'm thinking a textured plane with an SVG eye graphic placed symmetrically on the skull's front sides.

I'm checking the math to make sure the eye positions land right on the skull sphere's surface, adjusting for a slight outward offset so they don't clip inward, and planning the eye plane's tilt and size along with an almond-shaped amber eye texture with a slit pupil.

For mirroring, I'll draw separate left/right SVGs with a flip transform rather than negative-scaling the plane, since that flips face normals. Then for the ears, I'm extruding a triangular outline tilted slightly outward and forward, adding a smaller cream-colored inner ear shape offset slightly ahead of it.

Then I'll paint the ear tips dark by checking the extrusion's local y-coordinate, adding a ring of small spike extrusions along the cheeks as fur tufts, and placing the red kitsune forehead marking as a decal plane angled against the front of the skull.

For the legs, I'm setting up four limbs with shoulder and foot anchor points, using bent segments so the front legs flex backward at the elbow and the hind legs flex forward at the knee for a digitigrade fox stance.

Still adding leg details...

For the nine tails, I'm fanning them from the rump with each one spread across roughly a 70-degree arc, curving each path upward from base through a mid-point to the tip using an arc direction based on its angle index.

Adding fluffy color bands to the tails, gradient from coat color to white at the tips, then topping each tail with a small glowing blue spirit flame shape.

Defining the flame outline...

I'll use smoothing level 1 for a softer flame shape while keeping the tip sharp, checking the curve doesn't self-cross. For floating hitodama orbs, I'm planning five glowing spheres with small flame tops hovering around the body in a ring at roughly 0.8 radius, attached near the spine.

For the coat design, I'm leaning toward a white-silver fur base with crimson kumadori-style markings and gold accents, giving countershading on the belly using a cream tone applied at a mild negative level, with tail tips kept pale against darker crimson-black leg stockings.

For the neck, I'm planning a rope or collar accessory with shide paper, built by sweeping a tube shape around the neck bone and skinning it via a loop operation anchored to the neck joint frame.

Still working out the bell placement...

I should also add decorative elements: a golden crescent medal on the chest, forehead diamond decal, flame markings, and red stripe details on the legs, ears, and face painted onto the head part, plus eye-line accents.

For facial markings, I'll embed the red kumadori liner directly into the eye texture so it sweeps beyond the eye naturally. I'm skipping cheek decals but adding a nice touch of gold ring bands near the tail tip using a gradient sweep, and considering a small cluster of chest fluff spikes pointing down-forward for texture.

Still working out spike placement...

Now I'm verifying head geometry: body ending at chest, neck leading up to head center, and muzzle built as a capsule extending forward from the skull.

Still positioning facial features...

Now I'm verifying the leg and paw geometry sits correctly on the floor, checking that limb segments and sweep caps reach down to roughly y=0 without clipping, and sketching the front limb target position for a .58 total reach.

I'm tallying joint counts across spine, neck, head, jaw, legs, and tail, confirming each has an appropriate role assignment, and laying out the catmull spline control points for the spine chain path.

Then I work out the neck path extending from the spine's endpoint toward the head, placing neck1/neck2 joints and determining the head joint's position and orientation at the top of the neck.

Now I'm positioning the hips as the skeleton's root, chaining the spine off it, and setting the hind leg root joints symmetrically on either side of the body. For the body itself, I'm sweeping a tube mesh along the spine chain with varying radii at each joint, defining a width function so the torso reads as wider than it is tall.

Adding a crimson spine stripe marking and leg stockings as separate paint layers, then positioning the ears with their own tilt and thickness extrusion off the head bone.

Shaping the ear outline with a sharp tip and smoothed base corners, then painting it with crimson tips over fur base and adding a pinkish inner ear patch via a smaller forward-offset extrusion.

Now I'm planning the eyes as outward-facing planes positioned at head-center offsets, each textured with an SVG: a crimson liner swoosh sweeping outward-back, an almond-shaped eye with gold gradient fill, a dark slit pupil, and a white highlight. I'm working out orientation so the right eye's outer corner points correctly toward the viewer's perspective given the mirrored x-offset.

Calculating a sample surface point and outward normal for the eye placement, then checking whether a flat plane of that size would sit flush against the curved ellipsoid or show gaps at the edges—leaning toward shrinking the plane slightly to keep it hugging the surface.

I'm also positioning the forehead marking: finding the sphere point and normal at the top-front of the skull, offsetting outward slightly, and setting up a small crimson diamond shape there.

Now I'm working on the shrine rope and shide paper: a straw-colored rope swept around the neck at the collar, with white zigzag-outlined paper strips hanging down from the front center of the rope.

Trying to find the right surface hit point for hanging the shide in front of the neck, but the geometry is getting fiddly with the tilted rope plane. I'll just approximate by placing the shide near the nearest surface hit offset slightly outward and up, accepting some imprecision.

Now adding a small gold bell sphere at the shide's base, then placing five glowing spirit orbs around the figure with flame effects rising above each using crossing extruded shapes.

For the flames, I'm giving them a two-tone glow effect with a blue-purple outer layer and pale cyan inner core, anchored to the tail bones. I'm skipping extra details like rising wisps, gold bangles, and crimson leg markings to keep things simpler, and setting up the nine fanned tails and chest tufts with surface hit detection for placement.

Now I'm adding haunch and shoulder bulk using paint-colored body parts attached to the hip and shoulder bones, then working out the math for tail spread directions—using sine and cosine to fan them left-right behind the rump with varying elevation based on how central each tail is.

Still working out tail geometry...

Adding more paint functions...

Tracing the flame outline's remaining points counterclockwise to confirm no edge crossings near the tip's thin flick, then noting the smoothing level and placing the flame shape at the tail tip anchored to the last bone joint.

Setting the flame scale factor so tail flames render larger than orb flames, and adding a glowing orb sphere attached to the hip bone with its own flame positioned just above it. Then I'm sketching the cheek ruff spikes radiating outward from the head using mirrored side coordinates.

I'm now adding thin whisker rods from the muzzle sides, sorting out the imports needed from the builder kit, and starting to lay out the leg geometry with mirrored left/right root and foot points for the front limbs.

Defining more joint chains...

Adding more body parts...

Still writing eye SVG details...

I'll skip the pendant and move on to the neck rope and bell rigging, attaching the rope mesh via surface sweep and weighting bones from the path. I need to guard the neck loop and collar hit-test calls since they could return null if the joint placement misses the surface plane, then finalize the bells along the rope and write the final output.
